_comment: ACK LEDGER for scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh _check_launchd_agents (FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-PROBE-ACKED-LAUNCHD-DEATH-SUPPRESSION, 2026-07-23). A listed `label` whose launchd check currently fails (not-loaded OR non-zero exit status) is reported as acknowledged-degraded instead of a fresh failure: if every unhealthy launchd label found this run is in this list, the probe still returns ALL_GREEN (with the acknowledged labels named in `detail` for transparency) so the Tier-1 cron does not re-spawn system-auditor every ~30min tick re-confirming a signature that already has an open backlog fix-task. A NEW/unacknowledged failure (label absent from this list) always still fails the check, even alongside acked ones — acknowledgment never masks a fresh signature. STALENESS RULE: remove an entry once its `tracked_by` task reaches DONE_VERIFIED — a stale entry left here after the underlying fix ships would silently re-suppress a REAL regression forever. Read-only from the probe's point of view; edited by hand (PO/developer) when a launchd death gets triaged into a tracked backlog row, or when that row closes.

acked.label: com.vn-market.cowork-guaranteed-slot-firer
acked.signature: exit-status 143 = OUTER bound (b) of the tracked row: firer _bounded_exec SIGTERMs claude at FIRE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1800. Verified live 2026-07-25: firer.log 13:22:25Z invoking (bounded 1800s) slot=fb-weekend -> 13:52:25Z flow exited exit_code=143 (exactly 1800s); launchctl last exit code = 143. Same signature as the rows own reproducer (chef-morning 1800s SIGTERM 2026-07-22). ACK COVERS THIS LABELS non-zero-exit failures only in the sense the ledger allows (label-granular); a not-loaded/crash-at-startup failure of this label would also be suppressed - accepted tradeoff, mitigated by the STALENESS RULE above.

_comment_acked_memory: ACK LEDGER for the SAME probe's _check_mem_creep (FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-A30-MEM-SINGLE-CONTAINER-SCOPE, 2026-07-25). A listed `container` value is matched (case-insensitive substring) against the full name of any RUNNING, memory-capped container whose docker-stats MemPerc breaches WARN_PCT=85: if every breaching container this run is covered, the probe still returns ALL_GREEN (acked containers named in `detail` for transparency). A breach NOT covered here always still fails the check, even alongside acked ones — same mixed-case-never-suppresses guarantee as `acked` above. STALENESS RULE identical: remove the entry once its `tracked_by` task reaches DONE_VERIFIED. Seeded 2026-07-25 with rag-service, whose high steady-state (~94-98% of its 768m cap, healthy/serving throughout) is a detector-scope question, not a detector defect. CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (PO): the seed originally named RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND as the root cause of that steady-state. That was WRONG and is refuted by measurement — see the entry retarget_reason below. The driver is the embedder model singleton (fixed ~700 MiB baseline reached on the first embed), whose ceiling trade is owned by FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY, with the compaction failure-path counter defect owned by FIX-RAG-SERVICE-CLEAN-EXIT-RESTART-LOOP. ALSO CORRECTED: this comment previously implied the STALENESS RULE below is enforced. It is not — the probe reads only .container (auditor-tier1-probe.sh:275); tracked_by is never read, so an entry left here NEVER self-expires and NEVER narrows. Tracked by FIX-AUDITOR-MEMACK-HEADROOM-FLOOR-AND-DEAD-TRACKEDBY — do NOT resolve via a per-container threshold override (PO DECISION, task FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-A30-MEM-SINGLE-CONTAINER-SCOPE: static overrides are the same lagging-whitelist failure mode as FIX-AUDITOR-D4-WHITELIST-DATA-QUALITY-ANOMALY-PREFIX and would also silently swallow a REAL rag OOM approach).

acked_memory.retarget_reason: SCOPE MISMATCH + UNREACHABLE SELF-EXPIRY. (1) The prior tracked_by, RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND, bounds _build_fts_index(). It is NOT the driver of the suppressed condition: rag-service reaches ~97% of its 768 MiB cap after a SINGLE embed, with zero FTS activity, because apps/rag-service/infrastructure/embedder.py holds the sentence-transformers model as a lazy singleton with no release path (MEASURED by PO 2026-07-29T10:20-10:28Z: cold RSS 50.7 MiB -> 749.9 MiB after one POST /index; re-measured 745.8 MiB at 11:19Z after ~199 index writes, i.e. flat, no leak). Shipping the FTS row would not lower the number. That row own 2026-07-15 qa_result.idle_baseline_flag already said so verbatim: idle mem ~92% of the 768m bound with ZERO FTS activity — ten days before this ledger was seeded against it. (2) The STALENESS RULE is this ledger only safety promise, and binding it to RAG-FTS-BUILD-MEMORY-BOUND made it unreachable: that row is blocked_on rag-corpus-repopulation-to-representative-scale, PO-projected testable on/after ~2026-08-16, po_timegate_next_recheck_after 2026-08-12. The ACK could not expire for >=18 days by construction. FU-RAG-DEPLOY-MEMORY owns the resident-set / 768m-cap trade, so its DONE_VERIFIED is the event that would genuinely mean rag-service no longer sits at 97% of its cap. ENTRY DELIBERATELY NOT REMOVED: removal flips Tier-1 to FAILURE every ~30min tick and re-spawns system-auditor ~48x/day to re-confirm a known condition — the exact churn FIX-AUDITOR-TIER1-PROBE-ACKED-LAUNCHD-DEATH-SUPPRESSION was minted to kill. READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE FIELD: scripts/agents-flow/auditor-tier1-probe.sh:275 reads ONLY .acked_memory[].container. tracked_by is read by nothing, so this retarget changes NO probe behaviour and the STALENESS RULE remains enforced by prose alone. Making tracked_by load-bearing, plus an absolute-headroom floor the ACK may not swallow, is FIX-AUDITOR-MEMACK-HEADROOM-FLOOR-AND-DEAD-TRACKEDBY (backlog, P1).
